Chapter 257 (0254) Sanguosha's Concurrent Users Break 500,000

Besides the media, the game industry was also paying close attention.

Right now, the media's coverage of the online game industry was mostly normal. Local media would even praise local game companies. But as soon as some social incident occurred, they would suddenly lash out at online games, as if they were the root of all evil.

Even a newspaper of China Youth Daily's caliber had done an exclusive interview with Chen Tianqiao long ago, holding a completely laudatory attitude towards him and his company.

Only CCTV and People's Daily had consistently refrained from reporting on online game-related news.

The game industry needed someone to break the ice, which was also why Director Kou had helped.

Director Kou had wanted to do this for a long time but could never find the opportunity. Not without a sufficiently suitable reason.

It wasn't until Sanguosha invited students from Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan that Director Kou finally had a point of leverage.

These past two years were a special period.

Before the new leadership took office, even if Chen Guiliang organized a cross-strait student exchange event, the chance of it appearing on Xinwen Lianbo was extremely slim.

With the right time and the right event, everything fell into place.

"It actually made it on."

Chen Tianqiao sat in his office, looking at the dozen or so newspapers his secretary had collected. Deep down, all he felt was envy for Chen Guiliang.

He was the one most harshly criticized because of online games, yet he was also the one most concerned with public opinion. It got to the point where, after being scolded so much, he himself felt that making online games was dishonorable.

"Old Tan, come to my office for a chat." Chen Tianqiao called his trusted general, Tan Qunzhao.

Shanda started making games in 2001, but Tan Qunzhao had joined the company back in 1999. His current position was Senior Vice President of Gaming and Shanda's Chief Technology Officer.

Chen Tianqiao spared no effort trying to gain official recognition, but since it was inconvenient for him to come forward directly, he frantically tried to add halos to Shanda's head of gaming, Tan Qunzhao.

The year before last, Tan Qunzhao was named one of the "Top Ten Youths of the Shanghai Informatization Work System."

Last year, Tan Qunzhao was awarded the title of "China's Outstanding CIO."

This year, Chen Tianqiao was working on getting Tan Qunzhao the "Five-One Project Award for Outstanding New Cultural Talent."

This was the predicament facing the game industry today. The head of gaming at a major company was about to become a Five-One Project Award winner for outstanding new cultural talent. Yet the games he operated were considered unpresentable and were berated by the newspapers every other day.

"Boss." Tan Qunzhao reported to the office.

"Have a seat."

"Is it about acquiring the license for DNF?"

"No, I want to talk to you about something else."

Chen Tianqiao pushed the newspapers over, gesturing for Tan Qunzhao to take a look first.

Tan Qunzhao casually scanned a few of them and already had a general idea of the situation—the boss's old obsession was acting up again.

Chen Tianqiao said, "If online games are just about fighting and killing, it will inevitably leave a bad impression."

Tan Qunzhao said, "We also have casual games like Crazy Arcade and MapleStory."

"I'm saying, they need to have some cultural substance," Chen Tianqiao said, "something presentable, that can be put on display."

Tan Qunzhao tactfully pointed out, "Sanguosha was also heavily criticized by many people this time."

Chen Tianqiao said, "That's because they don't understand the game and are just mindlessly bashing it as if it's an MMO. We've grown very big now. It's indefensible for our company not to have a single work with cultural substance."

Tan Qunzhao reminded him, "We have Three Kingdoms Gallant Heroes. This game was independently developed for two years. Domestically, it's definitely a sincere major work with substance."

Chen Tianqiao shook his head. "I mean something with real cultural substance."

Tan Qunzhao thought for a moment and could only say, "Imitate Youke and make a Zhanguosha?"

"That would only make us a laughingstock," Chen Tianqiao vetoed at once, laying out his requirements. "It has to be original, with historical and cultural substance. Whether it makes money or not is secondary. Just give it a try."

Tan Qunzhao's head was throbbing. He already wanted to curse someone out in his mind.

"Is it hard to get on CCTV?" Shi Yuzhu said, holding a cigarette and crossing his legs as he read the newspaper.

If I want to get on, I'll get on!

Lin Hairui was quickly summoned by Shi Yuzhu.

This man used to follow Shi Yuzhu selling health supplements, in charge of promoting products like Nao Baijin. Now, he was in charge of promoting ZT Online.

Shi Yuzhu said to Lin Hairui, "I want to advertise ZT Online on CCTV."

"Huh? You can't advertise this stuff on TV," Lin Hairui reminded him.

Shi Yuzhu smiled and said, "It's like how tobacco companies do brand advertising. Don't mention the word 'cigarette,' just mention the cigarette brand. TV only bans cigarette ads, not brand ads. It's more or less the same for games. The game itself can't be on TV, but the game's brand can."

Lin Hairui thought it over carefully. "This method seems feasible."

"Go ask the people at the CCTV advertising department," Shi Yuzhu instructed.

After doing Nao Baijin and Huangjin Dadang for years, how could Shi Yuzhu not be familiar with the people in CCTV's ad department?

Lin Hairui took out his phone and made some calls, then covered the mouthpiece and said, "CCTV needs to discuss this matter."

Shi Yuzhu said, "I'll offer three times the fee for the same time slot."

Lin Hairui continued his call, stating their willingness to pay a triple fee.

Soon, the call ended. Lin Hairui smiled and said, "The person at the ad department said this can probably be done, but it does need to be reported to the higher-ups."

"Big organization. Going through procedures is to be expected," Shi Yuzhu said with a hint of disdain in his tone.

He knew those people all too well.

Throw three times the money at them, and as long as it wasn't illegal or against regulations, the CCTV ad department would figure out a way to solve any difficulties themselves.

Chen Tianqiao was still mulling over making a game with cultural substance to gain recognition from the authorities, the media, and the public. Shi Yuzhu was much more simple and crude; just throw money at the problem and be done with it.

Your Sanguosha got on CCTV?

My ZT Online can get on too!

Shi Yuzhu added, "Plan a promotional event where we pay players a salary for playing the game."

"Pay a salary?" Lin Hairui was confused again.

Shi Yuzhu nodded. "That's right, pay players a salary. As long as a player reaches level 60, we'll give them a salary of 100 RMB a month. Even free-to-play players who haven't spent any money can get it. Of course, we won't be giving them actual RMB, but in-game currency."

Lin Hairui immediately accepted the order and went to work on the promotional plan.

At this time, Shi Yuzhu's methods were still quite crude. He really just gave out the in-game currency that could only be obtained through topping up. Because of this move, the in-game economy of ZT Online was nearly brought to ruin.

Thus, he learned from this painful experience and hired economists to design a more complex currency system for ZT Online.

"What's the situation?"

"The highest PCU has finally broken the 500,000 mark!"

"Keep up the events and promotions. The tech and customer service departments will have to work a little harder. The higher the game's revenue, the bigger your year-end bonuses."

"Yes, Mr. Chen, we'll definitely work hard."

Sanguosha's PCU, on non-holiday evenings, was usually around 100,000-plus. On Friday, Saturday, and Sunday nights, the PCU could reach over 200,000.

If events were held during holidays, it could often surge to over 300,000 concurrent users.

And with the report on Xinwen Lianbo, coupled with the controversy in traditional media, this whirlwind of public opinion attracted a huge number of new players.

It shot straight up to 500,000 concurrent users!

Unfortunately, the spending habits of 2006 still leaned towards getting things for free if possible. This was true even for many players who had the financial means.

If this were after 2010, when more players were willing to pay, Sanguosha's revenue could have been several times higher.

Of course, this also had to do with Chen Guiliang being relatively conscientious.

The Wind Pack character cards, even if one didn't spend a single cent, could be collected by doing quests to get hero shards after playing consistently for two months.

By playing consistently for half a year without spending a penny, one could get most of the Fire Pack characters through quests—Xun Yu, Taishi Ci, and Yuan Shao were more expensive and would take at least eight months to collect.

And there were really people who, despite clearly not lacking money, would free-ride for eight months to collect all the Fire Pack characters!

To be able to free-ride for so long while maintaining their online time meant that even if they didn't spend money, they were loyal fans. For a game, these types of people were actually very valuable.

Besides being able to obtain character cards through quests, there were also frequent free giveaway events for Sanguo Shows, borders, and skins—mainly for outdated old items, like a clearance sale for last season's clothes.

Mr. Chen was truly too conscientious.

Good conscience isn't always repaid with ingratitude. This time, it paid off.

A player who had been a long-time member of the 17173 forums posted in the 17173 Sanguosha section: "Sanguosha: A Freeloader's Victory."

"I am male, a master's graduate from Huazhong University of Science and Technology, currently working at a state-owned enterprise. My salary is decent, enough to support my family... It's a bit embarrassing to say, but my family was poor when I was young, so I save wherever I can... Alright, I won't beat around the bush. I'm one of those freeloaders Mr. Chen talks about."

"I also played online games in school, mainly because I got envious watching my classmates play. But I always played only the free ones. When I reached a level where I had to buy a game time card, I would quit immediately. So, I've been on 17173 for several years, mainly browsing information on single-player games... and I download pirated single-player games too."

"In mid-April of last year, I got into Sanguosha. The reason I've been playing until now, besides the playability of the game itself, is because this game doesn't require spending money."

"As a freeloader, I've unlocked all the characters in the Standard, Wind, and Fire packs. I've unlocked 60% of the Forest Pack characters, with only Cao Pi, Lu Su, Dong Zhuo, and Jia Xu left. As for Sanguo Shows, borders, and character skins, besides the free ones, I've also obtained over ten paid ones each through event quests..."

"The user experience is excellent. Sanguosha is practically a freeloader's paradise. And am I addicted to the game? I only play for 40 minutes to an hour after work, for entertainment and to do my daily quests. Only occasionally, during a long drawn-out game, will it drag on for over an hour. For other games, one hour is nothing..."

"The groundless criticism from the media and the public, in my opinion, is just people with too much time on their hands..."

"Friends, cherish this game. If any other boss were running it, it would be absolutely impossible to get so much stuff for free..."

This post resonated with many players.

Netizens replied one after another, many saying they didn't have money.

Amidst a pile of replies, Chen Guiliang's verified account suddenly appeared: "Damn, so many freeloaders. I despise you all! [Impotent Rage emoji]"

The "Impotent Rage" emoji came from the recent sticker packs on Xiaonei Wang and Hainei Wang.

This thing was created under Chen Guiliang's instruction, imitating the AC Niang emoticons from AcFun, except the letter on the bun-like hair was different.

Of course, at this time, to insert an emoji in a forum post, one had to use an external image link. It wasn't as convenient as a single click.

But less than half a month after the emoji pack was released, it quickly became popular on Xiaonei Wang and Hainei Wang, and even began to spread to other websites.

"Haha, Mr. Chen is here. I freeload, and I'm proud of it."

"The term 'freeloader,' wasn't that coined by Mr. Chen last time?"

"Mr. Chen lets me freeload and feel good. Quick, lie down and turn over!"

"To the one above, I suspect you're posting something dirty."

"Let go of that Mr. Chen, let me at him!"

"Get in line, get in line."

"Mr. Chen is so busy entertaining guests, it's really tragic. I guess I'll pay a little something. I'm off to buy this year's full set of champion skins."

From the 1st of this month, due to the rise in public opinion, the 17173 Sanguosha section became incredibly popular.

It was catching up to World of Warcraft and Fantasy Westward Journey.

The number of posts and replies even surpassed these two games, ranking first.

As the first online game to be featured on Xinwen Lianbo, the website editors' rating would probably also increase. Combined with players actively voting and searching, on this month's 17173 online game monthly chart, Sanguosha was guaranteed a spot in the top three.

It even had a chance to aim for first place, taking down World of Warcraft and Fantasy Westward Journey.

The traffic brought by CCTV was immense!

If they could secure the top spot on the monthly chart once and promote it accordingly, even more players would be drawn to the game.

(End of this chapter)
